newsitem.title: KENYA: Sudan faces massive sleeping sickness outbreak.
newsitem.headline: Sudan faces massive sleeping sickness outbreak.

text.p: South Sudan faces a sleeping sickness outbreak rated one of the worst in the world this century, according to the results of a joint probe released on Friday.

A study by aid agency Care and the U.S.-based Centre for Disease Control found "catastrophic" sleeping sickness rates fueled by war in southern Sudan and a civil war in what is now the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
"If confirmed it would represent among the highest levels ... documented in this century," said CDC's Anne Moore in a statement.

The two-week survey in Tambura County, southern Sudan, in May found sleeping sickness rates in every village "more than two orders of magnitude higher" than those found less than a decade ago. The survey was aborted because of insecurity.

The disease, in which people literally sleep to death over a period of years, is spread by the tsetse fly. Controlling the fly is relatively easy but sleeping sickness treatment is risky and expensive, the report said.
